new_findings.issue: Now that the prologue is compact it shows that each comparison is constant: inside a function reached by the dispatcher, call.func_hash >> 224 is that function's selector, so with keccak taken as collision-free every term is false (pause) or one is true (unknown7b749c45).
new_findings.rule: Inside a function body reached through the selector dispatch, substitute call.func_hash >> 224 by the dispatched selector; sha3(p, Bytes(4, a)) == sha3(p, Bytes(4, b)) folds to a == b.

improvements: Owner-only prologue 100 lines of memory writes -> 11 lines and canPerform decoded (15 functions, each 130 -> 34 lines). Delegatecalls to the linked libraries now carry their arguments (onSwap unknown874b4782 x2, addToken/removeToken, f885a4bb); unknown90043a58's two dynamic arrays decoded; TokenAdded, GradualWeightUpdateScheduled and the fee-cache event show their data; removeToken/addToken keys are the token address instead of concat(mem[0]); SafeMath checks moved before the extcodesize require as in the bytecode; implied BAL#103 check and bounds asserts dropped (asserts 77 -> 52); P2 34 -> 10.
notes: Diff of 6,809 lines reviewed by function: calls and events identical in count everywhere; owner-only setters, onSwap, onJoinPool init path and removeToken read against the source. Hunk headers are misleading where functions moved (getActualSupply moved). onJoinPool BAL#000 1 -> 0 is the explicit check now SafeMath.add (same message); BAL#103 3 -> 2 drops a check implied by the first one.
summary: Clear improvement in the owner-only prologue, library delegatecalls and dynamic-array calls, but array accesses in the join/exit/token functions now spell out the whole free-memory-pointer sum, making those lines 3-4 times longer; plus a few new redundant checks.
